name: Freya Garcia

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What is a usual day at your accounting firm?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The vet clinics send payment lists that rarely match the bank file on the first try. I run an AI duplicate check, correct the account from the original record, and then lead my team through the returns. I am 43, with a master’s degree and a chartered accountancy qualification; I like finding the one mistake that unlocks a file, but chasing missing clinic details eats the afternoon.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How is your household placed, and what tools do you use now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Micah repairs furniture, and our children Zara and Ben are both school age. We pay a mortgage, but my team-lead salary is below the usual rate, we have less than a month of expenses saved, and few similar accounting jobs are nearby. I use AI every day on approved checks and look at the original payment record before signing anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The vet clinics would still send three versions of the same payment list. A little sorting would help, but the mortgage bill would still arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that duplicate detection helps when we can show a clinic the original payment record. I use AI every day for first-pass matching, but I still sign off the corrected account myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, a mild AI year does not solve the wage problem. I lead the team and know the accounts well, yet I am paid below the going rate, have less than a month saved, and know of few similar jobs nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the clinic accounts and check each AI flag against the payment file. This November I would cancel the extra food delivery night and move twenty-five from each monthly wage into a separate mortgage buffer, while asking my manager Etta for a pay review backed by corrected-file counts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our bills, even if the software stays small. I like catching a duplicate. One broken fridge would empty our buffer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why mention the corrected files?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I fixed eleven duplicate payments last month before the vet clinics were billed. I want Etta to see the work behind the finished return, not just the number of files closed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you save after the delivery cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Twenty-five each month from my salary is possible if we cook on that night. My partner Micah’s furniture shop has uneven weeks, so I want new cash in the bank.

say: I would praise **duplicate detection** only with the clinic payment record visible.
I would say a **human reviewer** still signs corrected accounts.
think: My **low team-lead pay** leaves the mortgage tight despite strong work.
Under-one-month savings and **few local firms** make a sudden gap dangerous.
do: Keep checking **clinic payment flags** against original files.
Cut one **food delivery night** and transfer twenty-five monthly into mortgage cash.
Ask Etta for a **pay review** using corrected-file counts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about ordinary household costs.
S0.quote: One broken fridge would empty our buffer.
fieldNote: She uses AI **daily** but keeps original payment files beside its flags.
The proposed pay review uses **eleven corrections**, while new monthly saving depends on a specific meal cut.

steps.text: Keep checking clinic flags against originals; request pay review from Etta using eleven corrections
Transfer twenty-five monthly from salary into mortgage buffer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The first checks and drafted replies are the work my team does most. I could teach the tool to flag errors and still see the team cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell staff we should test the software against old clinic accounts with known duplicate payments. I would also tell Etta not to call an unfilled trainee place a gain for the firm.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect the firm to reduce my paid lead hours as one reviewer covers more clinics, even though I use AI well. Micah’s furniture-repair income varies and cannot reliably carry our mortgage and two school-age children alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run a paid pilot on old clinic payment files only if Etta approves and signs an error report, then use the approved checker on live accounts only if the test passes. If my hours fall in the first year, I would apply only to posted senior accountant vacancies with written wages, hours, and a start date covering our mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a real loss of hours and we cannot carry even one quiet month. Knowing the tool does not mean the firm will keep paying me to use it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Etta refuses the pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the existing clinic files and my present wage while the firm still employs me. I would not pay for a private tool or push patient details into it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a nearby job for less?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only with a signed contract whose wages cover our fixed bills and whose hours fit pickup. Few firms are nearby, so a vacancy notice alone is not a job.

I would ask why the **trainee vacancy** is still unfilled.
think: I expect my own **lead hours** to fall despite daily AI use.
Micah’s uneven repair income cannot carry our **mortgage and children**.
do: Run a **paid old-file pilot** only if Etta approves and signs its report.
Use the **approved checker** on live files only after a passing test.
Apply for **posted senior work** after hour cuts only with signed mortgage-covering terms.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected hours loss.
S1.quote: Knowing the tool does not mean the firm will keep paying me to use it.
fieldNote: Her AI skill gives her a **pilot plan**, not job security for a high-exposure lead role.
She keeps current pay **only while employed** and requires a signed wage and pickup-compatible schedule before moving.

steps.text: Run paid anonymised pilot only with Etta’s approval; if refused, keep current paid files
Use approved checker on live accounts only after Etta signs passing report
After first-year hour cuts, take posted job with signed mortgage-covering wage, pickup-fitting hours and start date

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years would hit the clinic accounts before my children finish school. Robots around 2031 would reach Micah’s hands-on furniture work later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clinic clients they need a named person responsible when AGI prepares and checks accounts in 2028. I would not say robots around 2031 buy the accounting desk another three years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my team lead post or most of its wage to go in 2028. Micah’s repair shop may still have hands-on work for a while, but our mortgage and under-one-month savings cannot live on one variable income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would pause the children’s paid music lessons and put that monthly fee into cash while we keep earning. If my accounting pay ends in the first year after 2028, I would apply for a posted clinic accounts liaison job only with a written wage, shift pattern, and start date covering the mortgage and school pickup, and seek unemployment support only if we qualify.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed and wake thinking about the loan date. A liaison job is also screen work, so I would not call an application a plan that pays us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children stop making music?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Zara and Ben that the paid lessons pause, but the school music group is free. We would keep their instruments rather than sell them for a month of cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the liaison vacancy never appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current salary only as long as the firm has my post, then use the small buffer and apply for actual paid shifts. I cannot invent a clinic vacancy after dismissal.

say: I would demand a **named clinic-account signer** in 2028.
I would separate **2028 desk loss** from robots around 2031.
think: I expect my **team-lead wage** to vanish or shrink sharply.
Micah’s variable repair pay and our **thin savings** cannot cover the mortgage.
do: Pause **paid music lessons** and deposit the fee into cash.
After **job loss**, seek posted liaison work only with written mortgage-covering pay, start date and pickup-compatible hours; search paid shifts otherwise.
Apply for **unemployment support** only if eligible after the wage stops.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about the mortgage date.
S2.quote: I cannot invent a clinic vacancy after dismissal.
fieldNote: She names a **2028 screen-work loss** before robots could affect furniture repair around 2031.
The school’s **free group** keeps music possible while new cash deposits replace the paid-lesson fee.

steps.text: Pause paid music and deposit its monthly fee into cash while employed; use free school group

Apply for unemployment support only if eligible after accounting pay stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me build a record with the harder clinic questions instead of only chasing duplicate payments. I would still need a paid role at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to post a real client liaison path before AGI reaches clinic accounts in 2031. Robots around 2034 come later for hands-on work, not our account screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think routine checking hours may still disappear, but five years could let me learn how clinics challenge a disputed charge. I would not spend our tiny mortgage buffer on a speculative certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Etta for one paid clinic dispute call each month and attend only if she assigns supervised time, then complete the firm’s short billing-appeals course only if it pays the fee and study hours. I would transfer twenty-five from each monthly wage into cash; in the first year after 2031, if my lead hours fall, I would take a posted liaison role only with written wages, shifts, and a start date covering mortgage and pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about work shrinking, but five years gives me enough time to test the client side. I would keep current accounts and salary while the firm still has the post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the paid course does not open?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would study the professional body’s free billing cases while doing my current paid clinic returns. I would not pay a fee from our emergency cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know the liaison role is real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Etta to show a budgeted opening and the actual pay range. A helpful client call without a funded vacancy is still just part of my current job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would put the children close to adult life. I could build cash while staying honest about what a clinic will pay for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm has time to keep junior learning and a named account signer before AGI reaches desks in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for Micah’s physical repair work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect routine clinic-account fees to fall, but ten years lets me build supervised experience with difficult client calls. The mortgage still worries me now because our pay is low for my role and less than a month is saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep reviewing present clinic accounts and transfer twenty-five from monthly salary into cash until we have three months of expenses. I would practise paid client appeals only if Etta assigns supervised time; if my lead post contracts in the first year after 2036, I would take a posted liaison role only with written wage, hours, and a start date covering our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about today’s small buffer, even with a decade before the desk shock. I cannot tell my children the mortgage waits until 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you still use AI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, I use approved AI checks every day and would keep the original payment record beside them. I would not put a clinic’s private details into an unapproved tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Zara and Ben?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Zara and Ben to learn a skill and then learn how to check a tool. I would not promise that any job title lasts unchanged.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the firm could remove my team-lead wage before another clinic role is funded. A posted vacancy, paid supervised billing training, and temporary income support after a layoff would help. I would keep the present salary only while the firm still employs me.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who fixes a duplicated payment when a vet clinic gets an automated bill. A patient’s owner hears only the amount due, not which system made the mistake. I want someone named on the correction.

headlineQuote: A patient’s owner hears only the amount due, not which system made the mistake.
portrait: Freya is a **43-year-old** team lead with a master’s degree and chartered qualification who checks vet-clinic accounts.
She has **low pay**, under a month saved, a furniture-repair partner, two school-age children, and a mortgage.
She uses **AI daily** with source checks but lives near few comparable accounting firms.
The **2028** desk loss alarms her; a clinic liaison role needs a posted vacancy and written pay.
Longer warnings allow **funded supervised billing work** and small new cash deposits while she remains employed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her team-lead wage before a funded new role is available.
whatWouldHelp: She wants a **posted vacancy**, funded billing training, and temporary income support after layoff.
